subject: Telemetry archival tiers & Advanced Visualization pack — pricing and SLA tradeoffs

Subject: Question: long-term telemetry tiers & visualization add-on pricing

Hi Rafael —

We're evaluating Redwood for the inference layer and love the dev experience. Two pricing/packaging questions came up in our architecture review that I'd like to clarify before we proceed to the pilot stage:

1) Long-term telemetry: our product team needs searchable traces and span-level metrics for up to 3 years for audits. How do you price archival beyond the default 30/90/365d options? Is there a separate cold-storage tier, and does query SLA change for cold retrievals?

2) Advanced Visualization pack: we plan to use your dashboarding to build customer-facing health pages and internal capacity views. Is the visualization pack priced per seat, per dashboard, or by query volume? Any discounts if we commit to a 12‑month contract?

Also: is there an option to put a hard cap on monthly telemetry costs (burst bucket or credits) — our finance team prefers predictable monthly obligations for budgeting.

Happy to jump on a quick call this week. I’ve looped Monica from infra who will help with telemetry volumes.

Thanks,
Sana Riaz
Director, Platform Engineering
Stacksight

Hi Sana —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, then a couple of follow-ups so we can give a tailored commercial proposal.

- Archival tiers: we offer three archival profiles: 1) standard (30d), 2) extended (1yr) and 3) cold-archival (3yr+). Cold-archival is backed by compressed object storage and is priced primarily on GB-month and on per-retrieval queries; interactive queries against cold-archival have a higher per-query surcharge and longer SLOs (typically 99th percentile 6–12s depending on query window).

- Visualization pack: priced as a two-part model — a per-seat license for editors/viewers and a storage/query tier for dashboard backfills and historical lookups. We also include a small dashboard compute allowance for precomputed rollups.

Ballpark commercial framing (very approximate until we know volumes):
- Visualization seats: $200/user/month list (editor); $40/user/month viewer.
- Storage (extended): $0.045/GB-month; cold-archival: $0.012/GB-month + $0.02/GB retrieval surcharge (first 10TB discounted with commit).
- Query surcharge for cold: $0.30/query for raw trace fetches; aggregated rollup queries priced lower.

Options to control monthly spend: we support a budget cap with a burst bucket and automated throttling; alternatively, we can convert a portion of the committed monthly spend into "telemetry credits" applied to overage.

Can you share approximate weekly token/span volumes and how many team members need dashboard editor access? With that I’ll loop Karthik for the technical sizing and Monica for a committed spend construct. I’m attaching a short pricing table (pricing-table-v3.xlsx) with these ballparks so you can model scenarios.

If helpful, we can propose a 90‑day pilot: full platform + visualization pack for two editor seats and up to 5 TB of retention in extended tier at no charge — then convert to a 12‑month commit with discounts applied.

—Rafael

Hi all —

Quick technical notes that drive the pricing deltas Rafael quoted:

- Indexing & retrieval: raw span index size is the main storage/cost driver. If Stacksight plans to keep full-span payloads for 3 years, expect index growth ~3–5x compared to aggregated metrics. Cold-archival reduces on-disk index footprint by storing compressed blobs and a lightweight index.

- Query SLA tradeoffs: interactive trace search across cold-archival requires on-the-fly decompression + small-scale rehydration; that’s why cold queries are more expensive and slower. For dashboards, we highly recommend maintaining precomputed rollups (hourly/daily) for the last 90–365d and using cold retrieval only for deep forensic queries.

- Cost mitigation patterns: sampling (retain full spans for a subset of requests), pre-aggregated metrics, and synthetic rollups. We can also offer a hybrid pattern where you keep 90d of full spans and 3yr of compressed, index-lite traces.

I’m attaching an archival SLA matrix (archival-sla-matrix.csv) that maps retention windows to expected latencies and retrieval costs. Happy to run a sizing with your sample datasets if you can share a representative span export.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sana —

Appreciate the volumes — that helps a lot. Based on the numbers you shared we can put together a committed proposal with a couple of commercial levers:

1) Seat concession: 12‑month commit (minimum $80k MRC) -> 15% off editor seats, 25% off viewer seats.
2) Storage tiering credit: we’ll apply a one-time migration credit equal to 10% of estimated first‑year storage spend to help with archive conversion costs.
3) Query/overage protection: offer "Telemetry Cap" add-on — converts up to 20% of committed monthly spend into credits that absorb overage; alternatively we can do a hard monthly cap with throttling and an automatic escalation to a higher-performance tier.
4) Pilot concessions: confirm a 60‑day pilot that includes 2 editor seats for the visualization pack and 6 TB of extended retention at no charge; data used in the pilot will be counted toward sizing but not billed.

I’m attaching a formal proposal workbook (proposal-v2.xlsx) and a draft SLA addendum (SLA-draft.docx) that contains the cold-archival latency expectations and patch-retrieval SLOs. Key open items we need from Stacksight to finalize pricing: committed MRC target, whether you want the 3yr cold-archival for the 18% cohort or the hybrid (90d full + 3yr cold for selected cohorts), and decision on seat counts (editors vs viewers).

If that structure looks reasonable I’ll get Lauren involved on the commercial approval path and we can put this into a HubSpot quote (link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-78431).
